fallback.text: An emergency department over a 12-hour day: patients arrive at random (a Poisson stream, 8 an hour at the busiest), a nurse triages each one in 2–7 minutes, and doctors then see them. One patient in five is urgent and goes ahead of every routine patient; an urgent arrival even interrupts a routine consultation, which resumes later (pre-emptive priority). Routine patients who wait too long leave without being seen (on average after two hours). Each doctor needs about 18 minutes per patient on average, so 8 patients an hour already keep 2.4 doctors busy: with 2 doctors the queue grows, about one patient in five leaves unseen and the routine wait is over half an hour; 3 doctors bring the routine wait under 10 minutes but about 5 % still leave; 4 doctors keep those who leave under 1 %. The urgent patients hardly wait in any case: priority shields them from the crowd. The picture shows the doctors' queue over the day with 2 and with 4 doctors.
